title: U.S. Checks If TV Networks Broke Rules on Trump Coverage
summary:
The U.S. Justice Department is looking into several big TV networks. It wants to know if they broke competition laws when they briefly stopped sharing White House "pool" coverage of President Trump.

In a press pool, a few reporters cover an event and share notes or video with many newsrooms. Last month, five networks paused that shared coverage for several days. They did this after the government took away press badges from reporters at CNN, MS Now, and Politico.

Officials asked ABC, CBS, CNN, NBC, and Fox News for messages about the pool. They said a group pause might break a law called the Sherman Act, which stops companies from unfairly limiting competition.

A department spokesperson said the team is only investigating. The networks have not commented yet, the report said. Earlier, a judge ordered White House access restored after the outlets sued. The First Amendment protects press freedom.
why_it_matters: Shared news coverage helps families learn what leaders are doing, so rules about the press matter to kids too.
